Suppose the functor <MATH_0001> satisfies
the hypotheses of Proposition <REF_0001>,
and hence gives rise to a morphism of sites
<MATH_0002>. In this case
the pullback functor <MATH_0003> (resp.<SPACE_0001><MATH_0004>) and the pushforward
functor <MATH_0005> (resp. <MATH_0006>) extend to an adjoint pair of functors on
the categories of sheaves (resp.<SPACE_0002>presheaves)  of algebraic structures.
Moreover, these functors commute with taking
the underlying sheaf (resp.<SPACE_0003>presheaf) of sets.

We have defined <MATH_0001> above.
In the course of the proof of Proposition <REF_0001>
we saw that all the colimits used to define <MATH_0002> are
filtered under the assumptions of the proposition.
Hence we conclude from the definition of a type of
algebraic structure that we may define <MATH_0003> by exactly
the same colimits as a functor on presheaves of algebraic structures.
Adjointness of <MATH_0004> and <MATH_0005> is proved in exactly the
same way as the proof of Lemma <REF_0002>.
The discussion of sheafification of presheaves of
algebraic structures above then implies that we may define
<MATH_0006>.

<STRUCT_0001>
We briefly discuss a method for dealing with pullback and
pushforward for a general morphism of sites, and more generally
for any morphism of topoi.

In <REF_0003> this method is used. They introduce something
called an ``<TEXTITOPEN_0001>esp<ACCENT_0001>ce the structure alg<ACCENT_0002>brique <MATH_0023>d<ACCENT_0003>finie
